en.title: Brothers, sisters and cousins
en.summary: How to talk about your brothers, sisters and cousins.

paragraphs: Brothers, sisters and cousins are part of most family conversations. Here is a short description.

I have one brother and two sisters. My brother Jack is older than me, and my sisters are younger. Jack's wife is called Helen. My cousin Emma is my aunt's daughter. She lives in Scotland, and I visit her every summer.

**1. 's shows who a person belongs to.** Add 's to the owner's name: Jack's wife, my aunt's daughter. For the plural ending in s, add only the apostrophe: my sisters' rooms. See Introduction to Grammar: Nouns, kinds, gender and number.

blocks.html:
PatternExample
singular ownerJack's wife
plural ownermy sisters' rooms
two ownersJack and Helen's house

paragraphs: **2. Older and younger compare people.** Use than to name the second person: Jack is older than me. After than in everyday speech, we say me, not I. See Introduction to Grammar: Adjectives and comparison.

items: **Siblings** means brothers and sisters together. **Cousin** is used for both a boy and a girl.
**Elder** is a formal word for older and is used mostly before a noun: **my elder brother**.
We say **one brother and two sisters**, not one brother and two sister.

paragraphs: English has no special words for a mother's side or a father's side. Aunt, uncle and cousin are used on both sides of the family.
